question.name: CSEC Phy Jan 2023 Q6d(ii) — Polonium-210 Half-Life
question.text:
Polonium-210 has a half-life of 138 days. At a certain time, a sample contains 6.4 × 10⁶ polonium nuclei.

Calculate the number of polonium nuclei remaining after 552 days.
question.general_feedback:
Model solution:
Step 1: Number of half-lives = 552 ÷ 138 = 4
Step 2: N = N₀ × (½)ⁿ = 6.4 × 10⁶ × (0.5)⁴ = 6.4 × 10⁶ × 0.0625 = 400 000

Common errors: multiplying by n instead of raising ½ to the power n; computing ½ × 4 = 2 instead of (½)⁴ = 0.0625.

steps.label:
Given: Half-life t½ = 138 days  |  N₀ = 6.4 × 10⁶ nuclei  |  Total time = 552 days
Formula: N = N₀ × (½)ⁿ   where n = number of half-lives elapsed
How many half-lives have elapsed in 552 days? (1 mark)
Calculate the number of polonium nuclei remaining. (2 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: Divide the total time (552 days) by the half-life (138 days). 552 ÷ 138 = 4
Check: (½)⁴ = 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 × 0.5 = 0.0625. Do not multiply ½ × 4 — that gives the wrong answer.
error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: The formula is N = N₀ × (½)ⁿ. Raise ½ to the power of n (not multiply by n).
